doi_repair.basis: Round-2 recovery high confidence: CrossRef search for pea-protein-isolate volatiles vs extraction pH surfaced this paper; the Semantic Scholar abstract lists the nine semi-quantified compounds and includes all three the repo names - hexanal, 2-pentylfuran and 2,5-dimethylpyrazine - and states 'hexanal release was found 59% higher with extraction using pH 4.5 than with pH 6.5', matching the repo's pH-series anchor. pea_protein.citation_caveat: The cited author is wrong: this is Fischer et al., not Karolkowski et al. Karolkowski et al. (2021) is 'Volatile Compounds in Pulses: A Review', Foods 10:3140 (10.3390/foods10123140) - a review with no pH-resolved dataset, i.e. the DOI currently in the repo. I confirmed pH 4.5 and 6.5 from the abstract; the third level (pH 2.0) and the explicit LOD/LOQ table are stated only as 'acidic pH' / 'external calibration' in the abstract and were not verified line-by-line.

source_status_repair.basis: The dead DOI 10.1016/j.foodchem.2015.00000 is a placeholder pattern (all-zero article number), i.e. never a real identifier. CrossRef searches for soy-protein-isolate binding/retention of 2-methyl-3-furanthiol with pH and HS-SPME, and an author sweep of Fadel in Food Chemistry 2013-2017, return nothing reporting a percentage retention of MFT by soy isolate at pH 4.0 / 40 C. I could find no publication containing the '47.78% retention' anchor. | Two real 2015 Fadel papers exist and are the plausible confabulation seeds, but neither supports the claim: Lotfy, Fadel, El-Ghorab & Shaheen (2015), Food Chem. 187:7-13, 10.1016/j.foodchem.2015.04.027 (encapsulated beef-like flavourings from mushroom-protein hydrolysate - wrong matrix); and Fadel et al. (2015), Int. J. Food Process. Technol. 2:17-25, 10.15379/2408-9826.2015.02.01.3 (encapsulated meat-like flavouring from acid-hydrolysed soybean protein, in which MFT is the major fresh-sample compound and declines over 6 months' storage - but it is a gum-arabic encapsulation storage study with no pH series, no 40 C isotherm and no 47.78% figure).

doi_repair.basis: Round-2 recovery high confidence: CrossRef author search 'Siripitakpong' returns exactly one 2026 paper, and its Europe PMC full text (PMC12966641) contains the repo's three anchors verbatim: 'The delta-G values observed for vanillin bound to PPI are -9.05, -9.06, and -9.72 kcal/mol at 5 C, 15 C, and 25 C' (so -9.72 kcal/mol at 25.0 C), with all binding experiments in 0.05 M phosphate buffer at pH 7.0, on pea protein isolate, supported by AutoDock Vina molecular docking. This is unambiguously the paper the entry was built from.

pea_protein.citation_caveat: IMPORTANT: the ligand is VANILLIN, not 2-furfurylthiol - the word 'furfuryl' does not occur anywhere in the paper. The entry's compounds_supported ('2-furfurylthiol') is therefore wrong and the -9.72 kcal/mol value must not be used as an FFT binding energy. Also note -9.72 kcal/mol is the thermodynamic delta-G from binding isotherms, not the docking score (the docking affinities are -3.9689 kcal/mol for PPI and -3.7660 for deamidated PPI), so the entry's note 'obtained via molecular docking and homology modeling' is also inaccurate.
